transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hiya, um, thanks for calling S-Net TV and entertainment support, this is Megan speaking. How can I help you tonight?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Megan, it's Tariq here. Look, my S-Net Vision 4K set-top box is stuck in a continuous reboot loop with error code CS-104 and I'm missing the live Champions League match!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh no, Tariq, I am so sorry you're missing the football match tonight—I completely understand how frustrating it is when the TV box acts up right at kick-off.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, um, I sat down twenty minutes ago to watch the build-up on S-Net Sports Ultra, and the box just keeps flashing the S-Net logo, showing error CS-104, and restarting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, let's see what we can do to get your TV box working. So just to put that in my own words, instead of loading your live channels, your Vision 4K box repeatedly restarts after flashing error CS-104 on screen—have I got that right, Tariq?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's exactly what's happening, and even before it started looping earlier today, two of my sports channels were showing as unsubscribed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for confirming that, Tariq. Before I even open the account database, let's check the physical cabling and power setup around your television while we talk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, I'm crouching right in front of the TV cabinet in the living room now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. First question, how is the Vision 4K box connected to your electrical mains—is it plugged straight into the wall socket or into a multi-way extension strip?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Um, it's plugged into a six-way surge protector strip behind the cabinet along with the television and the soundbar.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, sometimes surge strips can drop voltage slightly when the internal hard drive spins up. And how does the box get its internet signal from your router—Wi-Fi or an Ethernet cable?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's connected with a yellow Ethernet cable going straight into the back of the router on the shelf above.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good, a wired Ethernet connection rules out wireless dropouts. What about the HDMI cable—is it plugged into the HDMI 1 or HDMI eARC port on your TV?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's in HDMI 2, which is the 4K 120 hertz port on my Sony television, using the original high-speed cable that came in the S-Net box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And do you have an optical audio cable or external USB drive plugged into the rear panel of the set-top box?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There's a digital optical cable going to the soundbar, uh, nothing in the USB port at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, let's try isolating the power draw first, Tariq. Can you unplug the optical cable for a moment and move the power plug from the extension strip directly into the wall socket?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hang on, let me reach behind the unit... okay, I've pulled the optical lead out and plugged the power brick straight into the wall socket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now switch the wall socket back on and tell me what colours the front LED bar goes through as it powers up.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, switching it on now... the front bar is solid amber, now it's pulsing white, and the S-Net Vision splash screen is on the TV.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Keep watching the screen—does it reach the loading programme guide bar at the bottom, or does it freeze at a certain percentage?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The little blue bar at the bottom got to thirty-five percent, stalled for a few seconds, flashed the error box, and clicked off again!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thirty-five percent is right where the box mounts the internal recording partition and downloads the conditional access entitlement file.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we do some kind of factory reset or forced software recovery without wiping all my recorded programmes?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There is a two-stage maintenance menu we can try booting into using the physical standby button on the side of the box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, how do we get into that maintenance menu?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we trigger the maintenance boot and check your sports channel entitlements on my system, let me pull up your customer file. What is the first line of your home address and your four-digit security PIN, Tariq?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, it's 19 Brampton Road, Birmingham, and my four-digit PIN is five five eight zero, 5580.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Lovely, got your account open now, Tariq. Hold on a sec while I look up error CS-104 in our technical bulletin database.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Alright, I'm waiting here by the TV.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, I found the bulletin on my screen. It says we should attempt a Soft System Restore from the engineering boot menu first.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, tell me what buttons to press on the box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Switch the power off at the wall socket, hold down the physical minus volume button on the side of the Vision box, and switch the wall power back on while holding that button.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, wall switch off... holding the minus button on the side... wall switch back on. My finger is still holding the button.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Keep holding it until the front LED light flashes purple and red alternately, then let go of the button.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait... yes, it's flashing purple and red now! I've let go, and a black engineering screen with white text just popped up on the TV.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! You should see four numbered options on that black engineering screen, Tariq. What are the options listed?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Option 1 is Restart Box, Option 2 is Software Recovery Keep Recordings, Option 3 is Full Factory Wipe, and Option 4 is Disk Surface Check.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Use the channel down button on your remote to highlight Option 2, Software Recovery Keep Recordings, and press the OK button in the middle.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Pressed OK on Option 2. Now it says Downloading Recovery Image over Ethernet, please do not power off.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That recovery image is only about eighty megabytes over fibre, so it should download and verify within a minute or so.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah, the download percentage is moving really fast—fifty percent, eighty percent, one hundred percent! Now it says Verifying Partition Table.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While it verifies the partition table, let me check why those two sports channels were showing as unsubscribed earlier today. Let me open your smartcard entitlement page.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, the TV screen just went black to reboot after finishing the recovery download.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Are you still there, Megan? Everything went completely quiet on the line for ages.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, yeah, I'm still here Tariq, my system screen was just running really slowly while loading your smartcard history.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, well the box just tried to boot back up after that Option 2 recovery, got to thirty-five percent on the blue bar, and crashed right back into the exact same error!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh dear, it crashed at thirty-five percent again even after the recovery image? Wait, what was that error code on the screen again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: CS-104! I told you at the very beginning of the call it was error code CS-104!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, right, yes, CS-104, my bad, I closed the bulletin tab earlier when I opened your smartcard screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Come on Megan, the first half of the match is nearly over. What about Option 4, the Disk Surface Check, or can you send a signal from your end?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's try running Option 4, the Disk Surface Check, from the engineering menu just in case a bad block on the recording partition is stalling the boot loader.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I've held the side button again and I'm back in the purple-and-red engineering menu. Selecting Option 4 now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What does the Disk Surface Check utility report on screen as it scans the sectors?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says Media Partition 1 Healthy, System Partition 0 Read Error at Block 0x004F, Aborting Mount.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: System Partition 0 Read Error at Block 0x004F... let me re-open that engineering bulletin and check what Block 0x004F corresponds to.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, what does the bulletin say when System Partition 0 has a read error?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Um, reading the bottom of the engineering note here... it says if CS-104 persists with a Partition 0 read error, the internal solid-state flash sector where the DRM keys live has failed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The internal flash sector has failed?! Does that mean the set-top box itself is completely broken?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yeah, unfortunately when sector zero on the DRM flash chip goes read-only, the box can never get past thirty-five percent on boot.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What if we try Option 3 on the engineering screen, the Full Factory Wipe? At this point I don't even care if I lose my recorded shows if it gets the football on!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can certainly try Option 3 if you're happy to lose your recordings, Tariq, though the bulletin says Partition 0 is separate from the recording drive.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let's try Option 3 right now anyway—it's highlighted on screen, I'm pressing OK to confirm Full Factory Wipe.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, what does the screen show now that you've triggered Option 3?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says Formatting Media Partition... completed. Formatting System Partition 0... Write Protected Error 0x004F, Reset Failed!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yeah, Write Protected Error 0x004F confirms the internal NAND flash chip on the motherboard has locked itself into permanent read-only protection.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How does a box that is only fourteen months old suddenly lock its motherboard chip in the middle of the evening?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: According to the bulletin, a batch of Vision 4K boxes with serial numbers starting SNV-22 had a flash controller wear issue after the autumn guide update.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me look at the sticker underneath the box... yes, my serial number starts with SNV-2208! So it's a known manufacturing defect!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, serial prefix SNV-2208 falls under that batch notice on our technical database.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, is there any USB recovery stick or emergency firmware rollback we can try for serial prefix SNV-2208 tonight?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, once the hardware flash controller sets the read-only bit on Block 0x004F, neither USB recovery nor an over-the-air rollback can overwrite the partition.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What if I leave the Vision box unplugged from the wall for half an hour to let the capacitors drain completely?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Draining the power capacitors only clears volatile RAM, Tariq, it won't unlock a permanent hardware write-protect flag on the NAND chip.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And there's no secondary backup partition on the hard drive that the box can boot from instead?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Unfortunately not, the boot loader always checks Partition 0 first for the conditional access security certificate before touching the hard drive.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so the hardware inside this box is 100 percent dead and cannot be fixed remotely tonight?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's right, the unit itself has a permanent hardware fault and will need to be physically swapped out.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, just great. Okay, well can you book a courier swap or get a replacement Vision 4K box sent out to me for tomorrow then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look, our TV hardware dispatch team handles faulty boxes, that's not something I deal with here—you'll have to ring them tomorrow morning to book a swap.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, what?! Why can't you order the replacement box on my account right now after we just spent fifteen minutes diagnosing it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because I sit in technical diagnostics and the warehouse replacement portal is run by the hardware dispatch team, which closes at eight o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can't you even log the replacement order on the ticket or warm-transfer me, or put it in a queue so I don't have to explain CS-104 all over again tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'll type a note on your account saying Option 2 and Option 3 failed on CS-104, Tariq, and thank you for choosing S-Net tonight, but you'll definitely need to dial back in after 8:00 AM and pick option 4 for hardware.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hang on, don't hang up yet! What about my sports channels and the match I'm missing right now—can I at least watch S-Net Sports on my laptop or tablet tonight?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, um, yes, you have the S-Net TV Go app included with your package, though the Ultra 4K channel only works on the main box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When I tried logging into the S-Net TV Go app on my iPad ten minutes before calling you, it said S-Net Sports 1 was not in my subscription either!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait, let me look back at your smartcard entitlement screen... oh, the entitlement refresh I sent earlier failed because your primary box is offline.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So because the main box is stuck in a boot loop, the app won't let me watch the football on my iPad either?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It looks like the app checks the master smartcard pairing status on the Vision box, and since the box hasn't completed a boot handshake today, the app entitlement is suspended.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you override that app entitlement manually so I can at least watch the second half on my iPad?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, the hardware dispatch team has to pair a new virtual smartcard ID when they issue the replacement box tomorrow morning, I don't have an override button here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What about giving me a credit for the S-Net Sports pack this month since I can't watch the Champions League tonight or use the box until a courier comes?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Billing adjustments for loss of TV service can only be applied once the replacement box is activated and the outage duration is closed by dispatch.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the box is still stuck restarting on my floor, I can't watch the match on my TV or my iPad, and I have to call another department tomorrow morning?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yeah, once you ring the hardware dispatch team after eight o'clock tomorrow morning, they'll arrange a courier swap for the Vision 4K box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What number do I even ring tomorrow morning? Is it the same customer service number?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, just ring the main 0800 S-Net number on your bill and select option 4 for TV hardware and returns.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unbelievable. Eighteen minutes on the phone and I'm left with a flashing box and no football. Fine, I'll call them at eight in the morning. Bye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright, have a good night Tariq, bye.
